newsitem.title: LEBANON: Two Beirut bank shares hit new highs.
newsitem.headline: Two Beirut bank shares hit new highs.

text.p: Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce and Bank of Beirut hit new highs on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Monday and active trade in Solidere boosted market turnover.
Solidere B shares rose to $11.25 from $11 while Solidere A held steady at $11 on highly increased turnover of 203,792 shares against 91,649 on Friday and 77,217 a day earlier.
Total turnover rose to 403,922 shares from 234,777 on Friday for a value of $3,976,007 against $2,038,040. Friday's turnover was the highest last week.
The LIBX bank index rose 1.25 percent to 165.85. The LISPI general index rose 0.54 percent to 89.93 and the BLOM general index rose 0.69 percent to 971.47.

"Demand on Solidere is becoming more widespread and coming from different sources, countries, and most important, institutions," Nicholas Sawan, head of trading at Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest said.
"I don't think an expected rise in supply after Solidere shares go ex-dividend will bring the share down as strong demand should sustain its price," Sawan told Reuters.
Solidere shareholders approved a 25 cents dividend -- 25 percent up on last year's -- at their annual meeting on Monday. Company sources have said the distribution will be completed in mid-July.
Among bank shares, BLC rose to $19.75 from $19.625. Bank of Beirut also rose to an alltime high of $4.125 from $4. A block of 40,000 BOB shares changed hands on the BSE at $4.063.
"BLC will see some resistance at the $20 level which is a psychological barrier. Once it breaks it, we might see it rising quickly," Sawan said.
"As for BOB, it is still riding on positive expectations for the bank's mid-year results. As more people see the bank is doing well, demand for the share increases," he added.
Demand for BOB on Monday was over 300,000 against supply of 100,000 shares.
"I believe Audi will remain at these levels until its Global Depositary Receipts start moving up," Sawan said.
Audi's GDR BAUD.BY traded on Monday at $27 to $27.5 on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange.
Of the four listed industrial firms, Ciments Libanais was unchanged at $1.2812 on trade of 10,000 shares.
There was no trade in the other listed shares: Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
